message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical, Chemical, and Nuclear Properties**

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Atomic Data** | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Ionization energy (first) | 13.598 eV |
| | Electron affinity | –0.754 eV (negative, so it does not readily accept an electron) |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | Atomic radius | ~31 pm (covalent) |
| | Van der Waals radius | ~120 pm |
| **Physical State (STP)** | State | Gas |
| | Color | Colorless |
| | Odor | Odorless |
| | Taste | Tasteless |
| | Density | 0.0899 g L⁻¹ (≈1/11 of air) |
| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C (−423.17 °F) |
| | Melting point | –259.16 °C (−434.69 °F) |
| | Specific heat capacity (gas) | 14.304 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Diffusivity | Extremely high (fastest among gases) |
| | Solubility in water | ~1.6 g L⁻¹ at 25 °C |
| **Chemical Behavior** | Molecular form | Diatomic (H₂) under normal conditions |
| | Bond type | Single covalent bond (H–H) |
| | Flammability | Highly flammable; explosive mixture with air (4–75 % H₂ in air) |
| | Reactivity | Forms hydrides with metals; reacts with halogens (HX), oxygen (H₂O), acids (HX), and many organics |
| | Acidic/Basic character | Acts as a weak acid (forming H₃O⁺) or base (forming H⁻ in hydrides) depending on partner |
| | Oxidation states | +1 (in most compounds), –1 (in metal hydrides) |
| | Common compounds | H₂O, H₂S, NH₃, CH₄, H₂O₂, HF, HCl, H₂O₂, etc. |
| **Isotopic Variants** | Protium (¹H) | Stable, most abundant (~99.98 %) |
| | Deuterium (²H, D) | Stable, ~0.02 % natural abundance; heavier, used in NMR, heavy water (D₂O) |
| | Tritium (³H, T) | Radioactive (β‑emitter, half‑life ≈12.32 y); used in nuclear fusion research, radiolabeling |
| **Nuclear Properties** | Stability | ¹H and ²H stable; ³H radioactive |
| | Nuclear spin | ¹H: ½, ²H: 1, ³H: ½ |
| | Magnetic moment | ¹H: 2.7928 µ_N, ²H: 0.8574 µ_N, ³H: 2.9785 µ_N |
| | Applications | ¹H NMR spectroscopy; ²H used in deuterated solvents; ³H used in tracer studies and fusion experiments |
| **Miscellaneous** | Role in Life | Essential component of water, organic molecules, ATP, etc. |
| | Energy source | Hydrogen fuel cells produce electricity via electrochemical reaction with oxygen (water + heat). |
| | Environmental impact | Clean combustion (only water vapor); storage and transport challenges (high diffusivity, low density). |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Hydrogen is the lightest element** and exists as a diatomic gas at room temperature.
- It has **two stable isotopes** (protium and deuterium) and one radioactive isotope (tritium).
- Its **physical properties** (low density, high diffusivity, flammability) make it useful as a clean fuel but also pose handling challenges.
- Chemically, it is **versatile**: forms hydrides with metals, reacts with halogens, acids, and many organic compounds.
- In **nuclear science**, its isotopes are key for NMR, tracer studies, and fusion research.

Feel free to ask for deeper details on any specific property or application!
